info.name: Finora API v1
info.description:
Generated by backend/scripts/build-api-docs.php from `php artisan route:list --json`.
Do not edit by hand — regenerate instead, or the collection will drift from the router.

Set `base_url`, then run Core → Sign in; the test script on that request stores `token`
and `workspace_id` automatically. Every other request reads them from the collection
variables, so no token is ever pasted into a saved request.

Amounts are ALWAYS integers in the currency's minor units — 35000 with currency TRY is
₺350.00, not ₺35,000. See docs/openapi.yaml, schema `Money`.

item.name: AI
item.description: Natural-language capture, receipt and voice drafts, chat and insights. Nothing is posted to the ledger without an explicit confirm call.

request.description:
Ask the assistant

Tool-calling chat over the workspace's own data. The workspace id is injected server-side and stripped from any tool arguments the model produces, so a prompt injected into a transaction description cannot redirect a query at another workspace. `redacted` lists what was removed.

Draft a transaction from text

Turns a sentence into a proposed transaction. It is a PROPOSAL — nothing reaches the ledger until `POST /ai/drafts/{id}/confirm`.

item.name: Confirm a draft into the ledger

request.description:
Confirm a draft into the ledger

The only path from a draft to a real transaction. Any field sent here overrides what was extracted, so a user can correct the machine before anything is written. Confirming twice is `409 ai_draft_already_resolved`.

Regenerate insights

Recomputes the statistical insights now rather than waiting for the schedule.

Queue receipt OCR

Takes a document id — upload the file first with `POST /documents`. This is not a multipart endpoint. Work is queued; poll `GET /ai/drafts` for the result, or listen on the workspace job channel.

Queue voice transcription

Takes a document id — upload the audio first with `POST /documents`. Not multipart.

item.name: Alerts
item.description: Alert rules, delivered alerts, and per-channel delivery preferences.

query.description: Only alerts not yet marked read.

request.description:
List alerts

Scoped to the calling user, not the whole workspace.

Update alert preferences

Alerts falling inside quiet hours are DEFERRED until the window ends, not dropped.

Edit an alert rule

Edits in place, keeping the id. `type` cannot change: it decides which scanner reads the rule and therefore what `config` means, so switching it would reinterpret the stored config rather than edit it.

item.name: Assets
item.description: Owned assets and their depreciation schedules.

request.description:
Depreciation schedule

Year-by-year schedule. Over the full life the depreciation sums to `purchase_price - salvage_value` and the book value never falls below salvage.

item.name: Audit
item.description: Append-only workspace audit trail and the caller's own security log.

request.description:
Workspace audit trail

Owner and admin only. Append-only: entries cannot be edited or deleted through any endpoint, because a trail you can quietly edit is not a trail.

Personal security log

Sign-in, sign-out and failed sign-in for the calling user. These events carry no workspace, which is why they live here rather than in a workspace trail.

item.name: Banking
item.description: Banks, cheques and loans with generated instalment schedules.

query.description: `due_date <=`. Useful for "what falls due this month".

request.description:
Clear a cheque

Marks the cheque cleared and writes the matching ledger transaction. A cheque that is not in a clearable state is refused with `check_not_clearable`, which carries the current status in `details`.

Create a loan

Generates the full instalment schedule on creation. The principal parts across the whole schedule sum to the principal exactly, and an annuity closes at zero.

Pay a loan instalment

Paying more than the instalment's remaining balance is refused with `installment_overpayment` rather than absorbed. Note this endpoint reads the `idempotency_key` BODY field only — it does not read the `Idempotency-Key` header.

query.description: Rebuild the schedule. Requires a writing role.

item.name: Billing
item.description: Plans, subscriptions, trials and subscription invoices.

request.description:
List subscription invoices

Finora's own invoices to the customer. Not to be confused with `/invoices`, which are the customer's invoices to THEIR customers.

Get the subscription

Returns three top-level keys, not the usual one: the subscription, what it entitles the workspace to, and what the workspace is currently using. Every limit in the product is read from `entitlements`, so this is the authoritative answer to "can I".

Change plan

Downgrading below what the workspace already uses is refused with `downgrade_blocked`, listing each violated limit — the alternative would be deleting the user's data to make it fit.

item.name: Budget
item.description: Budgets across six scopes, and live budget status.

query.description: Point in time to evaluate. Defaults to now.

request.description:
Budget consumption

Live spend against every budget for the period containing `at`. A category budget counts its whole subtree, and transfers never count as spending.

Edit a budget

Edits in place, keeping the id. `currency` is not accepted: spending is measured in the budget's own currency, so re-denominating an existing budget would silently reinterpret every figure already recorded against it. A custom period is validated against the stored window, so moving one end cannot invert it.

item.name: Buildings
item.description: Buildings, units, charge issuance and collection, and building reports.

request.description:
Pay a charge

Partial payments are allowed; paying more than is outstanding is refused with `overpayment`. Honours the `Idempotency-Key` header, which takes precedence over the body field.

query.description: Only charges with something still owed.

request.description:
Issue charges for a period

Divides `total` across the units using the building's formula. The parts sum to `total` exactly. Re-issuing a period that already has charges answers **200** with `meta.already_issued: true` instead of creating a second set — the safe answer to a double-tap.

item.name: Business
item.description: Contacts, projects, sales/purchase invoices and payments.

query.description: Substring match over name, phone and email.
Only invoices with an outstanding balance.

request.description:
Create an invoice

Totals are computed server-side from the lines and re-checked before the invoice is stored; a mismatch is a `500 inconsistent_invoice_totals` rather than a saved invoice that does not add up.

Pay an invoice

Paying more than is outstanding is refused with `payment_exceeds_balance`.

Void an invoice

An invoice that already has payments cannot be voided (`invoice_has_payments`) — reverse the payments first, so the ledger and the invoice never disagree.

Project profitability

Separates invoiced from ledger-recorded amounts, because they answer different questions — what was billed versus what actually moved.

item.name: Capture
item.description: Inbound capture channels: text, bank SMS, QR and email. All produce drafts.

request.description:
Inbound email webhook

Called by the mail provider, not by a client — it uses a shared secret rather than a Sanctum token, and takes no `X-Workspace-Id`; the workspace is resolved from the recipient ingest alias.

Authenticate with EITHER:
- `X-Capture-Signature: sha256=<hmac>` — HMAC-SHA256 of the RAW request body, keyed with the shared secret. Preferred; checked first when present.
- `X-Capture-Secret: <secret>` — the plain shared secret.

If no secret is configured the endpoint fails closed with `503 capture_webhook_not_configured` rather than accepting anything.

Create an ingest alias

The full `address` is returned ONCE, here. Only its hash is stored, so it cannot be shown again — copy it now. Requires a role that can manage others.

Confirm a captured message

Posts the message's draft to the ledger, with any corrections sent here taking precedence. A message with nothing to confirm is `422 capture_nothing_to_confirm`.

Capture a bank SMS

Matched against the bank SMS patterns in configuration. A message that matches nothing is still stored, with `status: "unparsed"`, and still answered `201` — losing it would be worse than keeping it for review.

Capture free text

Produces a draft. Capture NEVER posts to the ledger directly — confirmation is a separate call.

item.name: Core
item.description: Authentication, workspaces, members and invitations.

request.description:
Sign in

**Two different 200 bodies.** With two-factor confirmed, this returns a CHALLENGE and no token — exchange it at `POST /auth/2fa/verify`. Without, it returns the token and the user's workspaces. Check for `two_factor_required` before reading `token`.

Sign out

Revokes the current access token only, leaving the user's other devices signed in.

Register

Creates the user, seeds a personal workspace with a wallet account and a three-level category tree, and returns a token. The `token` is shown once.

Invite someone

The plaintext `token` is returned ONCE, on this response. Only its hash is stored, so a leaked database hands nobody a working link.

Accept an invitation

Not workspace-scoped — this is how someone gets INTO a workspace, so it cannot require already being in one; the token identifies the workspace. An unknown token answers exactly as a revoked one does, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which tokens exist.

Current user

Carries `deletion` while an account erasure is scheduled — null otherwise. Without it a client could only learn about a pending deletion from the answer to the DELETE that started it, so the grace-period warning disappeared as soon as the app was reopened.

Change a member's role

The owner cannot be demoted (`cannot_change_owner_role`) and nobody can be promoted to a second owner (`cannot_invite_as_owner`) — otherwise an admin could lock the owner out of their own books.

List workspaces

Deliberately NOT workspace-scoped: this is how a client discovers which ids it may send in `X-Workspace-Id`.

item.name: DataOps
item.description: Workspace data export and account deletion.

query.description: Row limit. Default 50, maximum 200. Note this is a plain limit; no pagination meta is returned.

request.description:
List data exports

There is no `GET /exports/{id}` — poll this collection and pick your row out of it.

Request a data export

Queues a ZIP of the whole workspace as CSV, JSON and the stored documents. Amounts in the export are written as decimal strings, not minor units — a spreadsheet cell reading 35000 for ₺350.00 would be worse than no export at all.

Schedule account deletion

Schedules deletion after a grace period rather than deleting now. `purge_after` is the point of no return — state it to the user before asking for the password, and use the server's value rather than computing it hopefully on the client. `POST /me/restore` cancels it while the window is open.

item.name: Documents
item.description: File uploads and polymorphic attachment to ledger records.

query.description: Alias, not a class name. An unrecognised value is `422 forbidden_attachable_type`.

request.description:
Upload a document

Multipart upload. Size and mime type are both whitelisted; the limits come from `config/documents.php` rather than being hard-coded here, so this spec states the shape and the server states the ceiling.

item.name: Attach a document to a record

request.description: Attach a document to a record

item.name: Detach a document from a record

request.description: Detach a document from a record

item.name: Family
item.description: Family members, spending caps and allowances.

request.description:
Update a family member

Currency cannot be changed after creation — an allowance history stated in two currencies would not be comparable.

Pay an allowance

Paying the same member twice for the same period is refused with `409 allowance_already_paid`, which is what stops a double-tap becoming a double payment.

item.name: I18n
item.description: Translation dictionary, served per locale with delta support.

request.description:
Override a translation

Overrides one string for everyone, without shipping a new build.

query.description: Return only keys changed after this instant, using the SERVER clock — a device with a skewed clock cannot miss an update forever.

request.description:
Get the translation dictionary

PUBLIC — no token. The sign-in screen needs its own words before anyone has a token, and a dictionary is not secret. A key with no value is never served: it would replace a working fallback with a blank label.

item.name: Investment
item.description: Investment positions, trades and performance.

request.description:
Record a trade

Buys move the weighted-average cost; sells never do. Selling more than is held is refused with `insufficient_quantity`. Honours the `Idempotency-Key` header, which takes precedence over the body field.

item.name: Ledger
item.description: Accounts, categories and double-entry transactions. The core of the product.

query.description: Restrict to categories usable for this flow. Categories of type `both` always match.
Return roots only, each with a nested `children` array, instead of a flat list.
Matches the category and everything beneath it.
Substring match over description, payee and notes.

request.description:
List transactions

Filtering by `category_id` includes the whole subtree — filtering by "Food" returns Restaurants and Groceries too, otherwise every parent category would read as empty.

Record a transaction

Posts balanced double-entry rows inside one database transaction.

`amount` is always POSITIVE — direction is carried by `type`, not by the sign. A negative amount is refused (`negative_amount`), as is zero (`zero_amount`).

This endpoint honours `Idempotency-Key`; the header takes precedence over the `idempotency_key` body field, because the header is what a retry layer actually sets.

Delete a transaction

Removes the entry rows and recalculates both affected account balances.

item.name: MarketData
item.description: Exchange rates and instrument prices.

query.description: Defaults to the workspace base currency.

request.description:
Exchange rate

Latest stored rate plus recent history. A rate that is zero, negative, non-numeric or more than ten times the previous one is rejected on ingest rather than stored, because a bad rate applied silently re-values every multi-currency balance in the product. If nothing is stored, a resolver fallback answers with `source: "fallback"`.

item.name: Payroll
item.description: Payroll

query.description: Match against name, job title or employee number.

request.description:
Create an employee

The optional `compensation` block sets the opening rate; omitting it creates an employee with no rate, who is then skipped by a run until one exists.

Update an employee

Pay is not editable here — a rate change is a new compensation record, so the history stays intact and a past run stays explicable.

Set a new pay rate

Appends a rate effective from a date rather than overwriting the current one. A run always uses the rate in force during its period, so raising someone's pay never restates last month.

Get a payslip

Lines are itemised by kind. A `contribution` is paid by the employer and is not subtracted from net — reading it as a deduction is the usual way a payslip gets misrendered.

query.description: Runs whose period ends on or after this date.

request.description:
Create a draft run

Calculates every payslip and posts nothing. An employee whose employment ended before the period is excluded even if listed explicitly, and someone who started or left mid-period is prorated by worked days.

`net` is `gross` minus `deductions`, exactly, in integer minor units. Employer contributions are not subtracted from net; they are in `employer_cost`.

Delete a draft run

Only a draft can be deleted. Once a run has been approved it has reached the ledger, and the way back is a reversing entry rather than a delete.

item.name: Approve a run and post it

request.description:
Approve a run and post it

This is the step that reaches the ledger, through the same `RecordTransaction` every other module uses. It is idempotent: approving an already-approved run returns the same run with the same transaction ids and does not post again.

item.name: Mark an approved run as paid

request.description: Mark an approved run as paid

Create a tax rule set

Brackets, contributions and fixed deductions are data, not code. A payslip records the name of the rule set that produced it, so amending a rule set cannot silently restate a run that has already been approved.

item.name: Recurring
item.description: Recurring transaction rules.

request.description:
Update a recurring rule

The schedule and the template are editable. Already-posted occurrences are never rewritten — a rule that has run keeps its cursor, so moving `starts_at` afterwards changes nothing about what was already posted and cannot replay or skip an occurrence.

item.name: Reports
item.description: Financial reports and their exports.

query.description: Start of the range, inclusive. Defaults to the start of the current month.
End of the range, inclusive to 23:59:59. Defaults to today.
Category depth to aggregate at. 1-10, default 1.

request.description:
Export a report

Answers one of two ways, and a client must handle both:

- **202** with a `ReportExport` record, when the export was queued — either because `queued: true` was sent or because the result is larger than the inline row limit for the format. Poll `GET /reports/exports/{id}` and use its `download_url`.
- **200** with the file bytes, when it was small enough to build inline.

Pass `queued: true` if you want an id you can poll and a link you can hand to a user; an inline export gives you neither.

item.name: Search
item.description: Lexical and semantic search across the workspace.

query.description: Comma-separated subset of `transactions,documents,categories`. Anything unrecognised searches all three.

request.description:
Search

Lexical search with Persian/Arabic normalisation applied at write time, so a query typed with Arabic ی/ک finds text stored with the Persian forms and vice versa.

Semantic search

Meaning-based search over a local concept lexicon, so "everything to do with the car" finds fuel, garage, insurance and fines across several categories without a network call. Results are a single ranked list, not grouped.

item.name: Security
item.description: Two-factor authentication and password reset.

request.description:
Confirm two-factor

Activates the secret and returns the recovery codes. They are shown ONCE — codes that scroll away unread are the same as no codes at all on the day the phone is lost.

Disable two-factor

Requires the password or a current code — at least one. Turning off a second factor must not be easier than turning it on.

Begin enabling two-factor

Issues a TOTP secret. It is NOT active until confirmed with a code — otherwise a mis-scanned QR would lock the user out of their own account.

item.name: Exchange a two-factor challenge for a token

request.description:
Exchange a two-factor challenge for a token

The second half of sign-in when two-factor is on. Accepts a TOTP code or a single-use recovery code.

Request a password reset

Answers identically for a known and an unknown address. A different answer would tell an attacker which addresses are registered.

Reset a password

Revokes every existing token on success, so a session an attacker already has does not survive the reset.

item.name: Sync
item.description: Offline-first delta sync and device registration.

request.description:
Register a device

Answers **201** for a new device and **200** when an existing one re-registers, so a client that repeats this on every launch does not accumulate duplicates.

Revoke a device

Revokes rather than deletes, and answers **200** with the revoked record — the row is kept so the audit trail still resolves the device that made past changes.

query.description: Return changes after this instant. Omit for a full backfill. Unparseable → `422 invalid_timestamp`.
Opaque cursor from the previous page's `next_cursor`. Tampered values → `422 invalid_cursor`.

request.description:
Pull server changes

Cursor-paged delta feed, totally ordered on `(updated_at, entity, id)` so no record can be skipped or repeated across pages. Follow `next_cursor` until it is null, then keep `server_time` as the next `since`.

Push local changes

Uploads a batch of offline changes and answers with one verdict per change, in order.

The rule this endpoint exists to enforce: **a disagreement about an amount, currency, account or date is never auto-resolved.** It comes back as `status: "conflict"` with the server's version in `server_payload`, for a person to settle. Non-financial fields merge last-write-wins.

`base_version` is the `version` the client last saw. A stale one is what makes a conflict detectable at all.

item.name: Travel
item.description: Trips, split expenses and settlement.

request.description:
Record a split expense

How the split is computed depends on `mode`:

- `equal` — divided evenly between the participants
- `percent` — `participants[].percent`, which must sum to 100
- `weight` — `participants[].weight`
- `exact` — `participants[].amount`, which must sum to `amount`

In every mode the shares sum to `amount` exactly: a remainder is handed out one minor unit at a time rather than rounded away, so splitting 100 three ways gives 34/33/33.

Settle a trip

Records the transfers from the preview. Every member ends at zero — a residue would be `unbalanced_trip`, a 500, because the arithmetic is not allowed to leak.

Preview settlement

Who owes what, and the smallest set of transfers that clears it — at most n-1 transfers, by greedy largest-creditor pairing. Nothing is written.
